What is my total upfront visa cost for a one-year master's?

For a typical 1-year master's, your total upfront visa costs would be approximately £558 + £776–£1,552 = £1,334–£2,110. A 3-year undergraduate degree would cost approximately £558 + £2,328–£3,104 = £2,886–£3,662 in visa fees and IHS alone. Add the TB test, any English test, your university deposit and your flights, and a realistic one-year budget needs to be built far higher than the visa fee alone suggests.

Do dependants pay the same visa and IHS fees?

If you are bringing a spouse, civil partner, or dependent child, each person must pay their own visa application fee (£558 each) and their own IHS at the same student rate (£776 per year). There is no family or bundled discount. Only students studying at PhD level or certain postgraduate research programmes can typically bring dependants — see the dependants section below.

Can I pay the visa fee in instalments or get it refunded?

No. The £558 application fee and the IHS are both paid online by debit or credit card at the point of application, and neither is refundable even if your application is refused or you withdraw it. Budget them as a fixed, non-recoverable cost from the moment you sit down to apply.

English language requirement

To obtain a Student visa, you must demonstrate English language ability at CEFR Level B2 (approximately IELTS 5.5–6.5 depending on the skill) for degree-level study. Your university specifies the exact level it requires on your CAS.

How do I prove my English language ability?

There are several ways to satisfy the requirement:

  • Secure English Language Test (SELT): Take an approved test such as IELTS for UKVI (Academic), PTE Academic UKVI, TOEFL iBT (home edition not accepted for visa purposes), or Trinity College London ISE II. The test must be taken at a UKVI-approved test centre. Most Pakistani universities require an overall score of 6.0–6.5 with no individual band below 5.5–6.0.
  • University-assessed English: Your university can assess your English ability itself — through a recognised test result, a Medium of Instruction (MOI) letter from your previous institution, or its own internal assessment — and confirm this on your CAS. If your CAS confirms that the university assessed your English, you do not need a separate SELT for the visa application.
  • Degree taught in English: If you hold a bachelor's degree or higher that was taught entirely in English, this may satisfy the requirement. This is more commonly accepted at master's level and above.
  • Nationality exemption: Citizens of majority English-speaking countries (e.g., USA, Canada, Australia, Ireland) are exempt. Pakistani nationals are not exempt.

Which English test should Pakistani students take?

IELTS for UKVI (Academic) is the most widely accepted and the safest option. It is offered by both the British Council and IDP Pakistan at centres across the country. PTE Academic UKVI is a growing alternative — it is computer-delivered and results are typically available within 2–5 days. TOEFL iBT is accepted by many universities but confirm that the home edition is not valid for UKVI purposes — you must take it at an official test centre.

Book your test early. Slots in Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi fill up quickly, especially in the months leading up to the September intake (May–July). Budget approximately PKR 50,000–80,000 for the test fee, depending on the provider.

Financial requirement — the most critical section

Financial evidence is the number one reason for UK student visa refusals from Pakistan, accounting for roughly 40% of all rejections. The rules are strict, specific, and unforgiving. You must prove you can cover both your tuition fees and your living costs, and you must do so in a very specific way.

How much money must I show in my bank account?

You must demonstrate that you have access to:

  • First-year tuition fees: The exact amount stated on your CAS, minus any deposit you have already paid and which is recorded on the CAS.
  • Living costs (maintenance funds): Calculated based on where you will study:
Study LocationMonthly RateMaximum (9 months)
London (City of London + 32 boroughs)£1,529/month£13,761
Outside London (rest of England, Wales, Scotland, NI)£1,171/month£10,539

These rates were updated in January 2025 and remain in force through 2026. They represent a significant increase from the previous rates (£1,334/£1,023 per month). Older guides may quote the old figures — always verify on gov.uk/student-visa/money.

What does that look like in a worked example?

Suppose you have been accepted for a 1-year MSc at a university in Manchester (outside London). Your CAS states a tuition fee of £16,000, and you have already paid a £3,000 deposit. Your financial requirement is:

  • Outstanding tuition: £16,000 − £3,000 = £13,000
  • Maintenance funds: £1,171 × 9 months = £10,539
  • Total required: £23,539

You must show at least £23,539 in your bank account (or a combination of your own and a sponsor's account). UKVI converts your funds to GBP using the OANDA exchange rate on the date of your application, not the date of your bank statement. If the Pakistani rupee weakens between your statement date and your application date, your balance might fall short. Add a 5–10% buffer above the minimum to protect against currency fluctuation.

What exactly is the 28-day rule?

This is the rule that catches the most applicants. Your funds must have been held in an eligible account for 28 consecutive days, with the last day of the 28-day period falling within 31 days of the date you submit your visa application. In practice, this means:

  • Your bank statement must cover at least 28 days.
  • On every single day of those 28 days, the balance must be at or above the required amount. Not just the opening and closing balance — every day.
  • If the balance dips below the required amount on even one day — even briefly, even due to a fee deduction — the clock resets. You must start the 28-day period again.
  • The closing date of the 28-day period on your statement must be no more than 31 days before you submit your application.

How should I time my money so the 28-day rule works?

Work backwards from your intended submission date. Move the money in 45–60 days before the window starts, obtain stamped statements from your bank branch, and submit within a few days of the window closing. Applying on the last valid day of the 31-day window is unnecessarily risky.

What mistakes cause financial refusals?

  • Funds parking: Transferring a large sum into your account just weeks before the 28-day window looks suspicious. UKVI treats sudden large deposits as borrowed money. Move funds into the account 45–60 days before the 28-day window starts, so your statement shows a month of stable balance before the required period begins.
  • Wrong account type: Funds must be in a cash account — a savings account, current account, or accessible fixed deposit at a regulated financial institution. Shares, bonds, pensions, mutual funds, Sahulat accounts, National Savings certificates, cryptocurrency, and credit card limits do not count.
  • Unstamped statements: Printouts from online banking without an official bank stamp and letterhead are routinely refused. Get your statements directly from your bank branch, on bank letterhead, signed and stamped.
  • Multiple accounts: Splitting funds across different accounts creates complexity and increases the risk of errors. The cleanest approach is a single account with the full required amount.
  • No source-of-funds evidence: If a large deposit appears in your account, UKVI may question where it came from. Be prepared to show salary slips, business income records, property sale documents, or other evidence explaining the source.

Can I use my parent's or guardian's bank account?

If the funds are in your parent's or legal guardian's account rather than your own, you can still use them — but you must provide:

  • A signed consent letter from your parent/guardian confirming they are funding your studies and consent to the visa application.
  • A birth certificate or NADRA Family Registration Certificate (FRC) proving your relationship to the sponsor.
  • The sponsor's CNIC copy (Computerised National Identity Card).
  • The sponsor's 28-day bank statement meeting all the same requirements above.
  • Evidence of the sponsor's income or wealth — salary slips, business registration, property documents, tax returns — to demonstrate that the funds are genuine and not borrowed.

The bank statement must be in the sponsor's name, and the consent letter must explicitly reference your name, your passport number, the university name, and the course. A generic letter without these specifics is not enough.

What if the money is in a sibling's, cousin's, or partner's account?

This is where many families get caught out. The rules are written around parents, legal guardians, partners who apply with you or already hold UK permission, and official sponsors. A brother, cousin, uncle or grandparent is not automatically an eligible sponsor. If your funder falls outside those categories, get specialist advice before building your financial case around them.

What about a scholarship or official sponsorship instead of my own money?

If your studies are fully funded by a recognised scholarship body — such as the HEC Commonwealth Scholarship, Chevening, or a university scholarship — the scholarship letter must confirm the amount of tuition and living costs covered, the duration, and the name of the sponsoring body. If the scholarship covers all your costs, you may not need to provide personal bank statements. However, UKVI may still request financial evidence after submission, so keep your documents ready regardless.

Can I use a government loan letter instead of bank statements?

You can also use an official sponsor's funds (e.g., a government scholarship, HEC, British Council, or university scholarship). Student loan letters from government or government-sponsored loan companies are also accepted. The letter must come from the institution itself, be recent, and state the amount available — a self-drafted promissory note from a family friend is not a loan letter.

Am I exempt from providing financial evidence?

You do not need to provide financial evidence if:

  • You have been in the UK on a valid visa for at least 12 months on the date of your application (in-country applications only).
  • You are a Student Union Sabbatical Officer.
  • You are a doctor or dentist in postgraduate training.

As a Pakistani applicant applying from outside the UK, you almost certainly do need to provide financial evidence. There is no exemption for Pakistani nationals.

Why does the Home Office check my bank with my bank directly?

UKVI can contact the issuing bank to confirm that a statement is genuine, that the account is in the named holder's name, and that the balance history is accurate. This is why printed screenshots and self-edited PDFs are discovered quickly. A bank-issued, stamped statement obtained directly from a branch needs no explanation, and it is the single cheapest way to remove risk from your application.

Age requirement and parental consent

You must be 16 or over when you apply. If you are 16 or 17 years old, you need:

  • Written consent from both parents (or the person with sole or joint parental responsibility).
  • The consent letter must confirm that both parents consent to the visa application, the travel to the UK, and the living arrangements in the UK.
  • A copy of your birth certificate showing the names of both parents.

Do I still need parental consent if I am funding myself at 18?

If you are 18 or over, parental consent is not required, regardless of whether your parents are funding your studies. Age and funding are treated separately: the consent requirement is a safeguard for minors, not a condition of the financial evidence. Many 18-year-olds funded by parents therefore provide a consent-style letter anyway, which is harmless and occasionally helpful, but it is not mandatory.

Complete document checklist for 2026

This is the full list of documents you should prepare. Not every document will apply to every applicant, but this covers all common scenarios for Pakistani students:

  1. Valid Pakistani passport — must be valid for the full duration of your intended stay, with at least one blank page for the visa stamp. Include all previous/old passports showing your travel history.
  2. CAS reference number — from your university. You will enter this in your online application; you do not need to print the CAS statement, but keep a copy for your records.
  3. Bank statements — meeting the 28-day rule, on bank letterhead, stamped and signed, showing the required amount. Or a loan letter / scholarship letter / official sponsorship letter as applicable.
  4. Academic documents — all qualifications listed on your CAS: degree certificates, transcripts, HSSC / A-Level certificates, SSC / O-Level certificates. Originals or certified copies.
  5. English language test result — IELTS UKVI, PTE Academic UKVI, or equivalent. Only if required (check your CAS — if the university assessed your English, this may not be needed separately).
  6. Tuberculosis (TB) test certificate — from a UKVI-approved clinic in Pakistan. Mandatory for all Pakistani applicants. Valid for 6 months from the date of the test.
  7. ATAS certificate — only if your course requires it. The Academic Technology Approval Scheme certificate is needed for certain postgraduate courses in science, engineering, and technology. Your university will tell you if you need one. It must be obtained before you apply for the visa.
  8. Passport-size photographs — meeting UK biometric photo requirements (white background, specific dimensions). Some VFS centres take your photo at the appointment.
  9. Parental consent and birth certificate — if you are under 18.
  10. Sponsor's documents — if a parent is funding you: their CNIC, bank statements (28-day compliant), consent letter, birth certificate / FRC, and income evidence (salary slips, business documents, tax returns).
  11. Personal statement / Statement of Purpose — explaining why you chose this course, this university, and how it connects to your career plans. While not always a formal visa document requirement, it is critical for the genuine student assessment and may be requested.
  12. CV / resume — particularly useful for postgraduate applicants to show academic and work history.
  13. Work experience letters — if relevant to your course (e.g., MBA, professional master's).
  14. Family Registration Certificate (FRC) — from NADRA, if your family is sponsoring you. Useful for demonstrating family ties to Pakistan.
  15. Scholarship letter — if applicable, from the scholarship body.
  16. Certified English translations — for any document not in English. The translation must include the translator's name, credentials, contact details, date, and a declaration of accuracy.

What is the genuine student requirement?

Under paragraph ST 5.1 of Appendix Student, the UKVI caseworker must be satisfied that you are a genuine student. This is not just a formality — it is an active assessment. The caseworker evaluates:

  • Whether your course choice makes sense given your academic background and career goals.
  • Whether your personal statement demonstrates genuine motivation for studying this course at this university.
  • Whether you can explain your study plan in a credibility interview (if called).
  • Whether your financial circumstances are consistent with the study plan.
  • Whether you have ties to Pakistan that suggest you intend to return after your studies.

This is where many well-qualified Pakistani applicants fail. A computer science graduate applying for a master's in data science has a clear, logical path. A business graduate applying for a nursing course with no explanation of the pivot raises questions. Your personal statement is the key document here — see the tips section below.

Do I need a personal statement for the visa itself?

Not as a formal upload on the standard checklist, but treat it as if it were. The genuine student assessment is the reason a caseworker can refuse a well-funded, well-qualified applicant, and the personal statement is the document they read to judge your intentions. Prepare a version that names your modules, your university, and your plan for Pakistan, and keep it ready in case it is requested.

What about documents that are not in English?

Any document not written in English needs a certified translation, and the certification must include the translator's name, credentials, contact details, date, and a declaration of accuracy. Pakistani degrees, transcripts, birth certificates and NADRA documents all normally fall into this category. Sending an uncertified translation is one of the most common document-level refusals, and fixing it afterwards costs you another fee.

How to apply online — step by step

The entire Student visa application is completed online. Here is the exact process for Pakistani applicants in 2026, in the order you should do it.

Step 1: How do I gather my documents before I start?

Before starting the application, have all your documents ready: CAS number, passport details, bank statements, TB test certificate, English test score, academic certificates, and sponsor documents if applicable. You will need to reference these during the application. Anything you do not have to hand is a reason your application date slips, so treat step 1 as the real deadline.

Step 2: How do I complete the online application on GOV.UK?

Go to gov.uk/student-visa/apply and select "Apply from outside the UK." You will create a UKVI account (if you don't already have one) and fill in the application form. The form asks for:

  • Your personal details (name, date of birth, passport number — must match your CAS exactly)
  • Your CAS reference number
  • Your course details
  • Financial information (how you will fund your studies)
  • Travel history
  • Criminal record declarations
  • Whether you have been refused a visa before (from any country)

You can save and return to the application later, but your application date is the date you submit and pay — not the date you start filling it in. Read every answer twice before you submit, particularly the refusal question, because a "no" answer there is far safer than an undeclared "yes" answer found later.

Step 3: How much do I pay for the visa application fee?

The £558 application fee is paid online by debit or credit card as part of the application process. The fee is non-refundable, even if your application is refused. Have your card ready before you start the form, because the payment step is what fixes your application date.

Step 4: How do I pay the Immigration Health Surcharge?

After paying the application fee, you will be directed to the IHS payment portal. The system calculates the amount automatically based on your visa duration. For a 1-year master's with a 16-month visa, the IHS would be £776 × 2 = £1,552. Pay by card and keep your IHS reference number — you will need it. Screenshot the confirmation page, because a failed payment can leave your application in an incomplete state that delays biometrics.

Step 5: How do I book my biometric appointment?

After payment, you will be directed to the VFS Global website to book an appointment at a Visa Application Centre in Pakistan. You must attend in person to provide your biometric data (fingerprints and a digital photograph).

Which VFS Global centres are in Pakistan?

VFS Global operates centres in three Pakistani cities:

  • Islamabad — Park Road, Chatta Bakhtawar, Chak Shahzad
  • Lahore — Ground Floor, MCT Madina Corporate Tower, 8 Queens Road
  • Karachi — 43/1/D, Razi Road, PECHS, Shahrah-e-Faisal

All three centres are open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with submission hours typically 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Book your appointment as soon as possible after submitting your online application — slots fill up fast, especially in Lahore and Karachi during peak season. Note that UKVI business days and Pakistani public holidays do not always align, so leave slack around Eid and Independence Day.

Step 6: What happens at my biometrics appointment?

On your appointment day, bring:

  • Your current passport (and old passports if applicable)
  • A printed copy of your application summary
  • All supporting documents — bank statements, academic certificates, TB test certificate, sponsor documents, English test result, etc.
  • The appointment confirmation from VFS Global

At the centre, your fingerprints and photo will be taken, and your documents will be submitted (either uploaded digitally or handed in, depending on the centre's process). Some VFS centres offer optional document upload assistance for an additional fee.

You may also be asked to pay a VFS service fee at the centre. Some centres include this in the appointment booking; others charge separately. Check the VFS Global Pakistan website for current details.

Step 7: How long do I wait for the decision?

UKVI will process your application and make a decision. Standard processing from Pakistan takes approximately 3 weeks (15 working days) from the date your biometrics are submitted. During peak season (June–September), processing can take 4–6 weeks. If your course start date is close, factor this waiting time into your travel booking rather than assuming the decision will be quick.

Priority and super-priority processing

If you need a faster decision, UKVI offers optional priority services for a UK student visa from Pakistan:

  • Priority service: Decision within approximately 5 working days. Available for an extra fee of approximately £500. Availability depends on demand at your VFS centre.
  • Super-priority service: Decision within approximately 1 working day. Available for an extra fee of approximately £1,000. Very limited availability in Pakistan — this may not be offered at all centres.

Is priority processing actually available at Pakistani VFS centres?

Availability is not guaranteed. Capacity for priority services is allocated by the visa application centre and changes week to week, so you may be offered it at one booking and not the next. Pakistani applicants are also subject to a cap on how many priority applications a centre can accept each day. If it is not available, you will simply receive standard processing.

Should I pay for priority processing or save the money?

These services are optional. Most Pakistani applicants use the standard service. If your course starts soon and you are cutting it close on timing, check whether priority is available at your chosen VFS centre when you book your appointment. £500 buys you roughly two weeks, which is rarely worth it if you applied within the recommended 8–10 week window in the first place.

Timing is everything. Work backwards from your course start date using the table below, and note that several of these tasks can run in parallel.

When is the earliest I can apply?

The earliest you can apply is 6 months before your course start date. Apply as soon as your CAS is ready and your funds are in place — and remember that your CAS itself expires after 6 months, so there is no benefit in holding a completed one open while you wait.

How late is too late to apply?

Arriving in the UK more than one month before your course starts can get you refused entry, and arriving after registration closes can jeopardise your place. As a practical rule, submit your application 8–10 weeks before your course starts. If you have missed that, the 3-week processing time plus a possible 4–6 week peak-season delay is your real constraint.

After approval — what happens next

Will I get a physical visa sticker in my passport?

From January 2025, the UK transitioned to a digital immigration system. When your Student visa is approved, you will not receive a physical visa sticker (vignette) in your passport in most cases. Instead, your immigration status is stored digitally as an eVisa. You will need to:

  • Create or access your UKVI account (the same account you used for the application).
  • Link your passport to your UKVI account using the "View and prove" service on GOV.UK.
  • Use the UK Immigration: ID Check app to verify your identity.

How do I prove my immigration status in the UK?

Your eVisa confirms your immigration status, work rights, and any conditions attached to your visa. You can share your immigration status with employers, landlords, and universities using a share code generated through your UKVI account. Every employer who hires you on a Student visa will ask for that share code and verify it online, so set it up before you start job hunting.

What happens when I arrive at the UK border?

When you arrive at a UK port of entry, present your passport and explain that you are coming to study. The Border Force officer may ask to see your CAS, proof of funds, or your university enrolment details. Carry a printout of your CAS and your university offer letter, even though these are stored electronically. Being able to answer questions about your course, your fees and your accommodation in a few clear sentences is what keeps the border interview routine.

How early can I arrive in the UK?

You can enter the UK up to 1 month before your course starts if your visa is for more than 6 months. Do not arrive more than 1 month early — you may be refused entry. Arriving far too early is treated as a signal that you do not yet have confirmed arrangements, which is exactly the impression a genuine student should avoid.

Do I still need to collect a BRP card?

In some cases, you may still be asked to collect a Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) card from a designated Post Office within 10 days of arrival. Check your visa decision letter for instructions. However, the UK is phasing out physical BRPs in favour of eVisas, so this requirement may not apply to all 2026 applicants. Follow the instructions in your decision letter.

Working rights on a Student visa

One of the biggest advantages of the Student visa is the ability to work while studying, which matters a great deal for Pakistani applicants who want part-time income in the UK and a head start on their career. Your work rights are:

  • During term time: Up to 20 hours per week (typically defined as Monday to Sunday).
  • During vacation periods: Full-time (no hourly limit). This includes the summer break, Christmas break, and Easter break as defined by your university's academic calendar.
  • After graduation: You may be eligible for the Graduate Route visa (2 years for master's/bachelor's graduates, 3 years for PhD graduates), which allows you to work full-time without restrictions.

How many hours a week can I work during term time?

The limit is 20 hours per week, counted across all jobs combined and measured over any seven-day period rather than a Monday-to-Friday working week. Exceeding it is a breach of your visa conditions and can jeopardise your permission to stay. Plan your hours in advance rather than averaging them out at the end of a month.

What counts as a vacation period for full-time work?

Official vacation periods as defined by your university's academic calendar, which means the summer break, the Christmas break and Easter break. Reading weeks and exam periods are term time, not vacation. If you are unsure whether a gap in your timetable qualifies, ask your university in writing, and keep the answer — employers sometimes misclassify periods as vacation when they are not.

Which jobs am I not allowed to do?

You cannot:

  • Be self-employed or engage in business activity.
  • Fill a permanent full-time vacancy.
  • Work as a professional sportsperson or sports coach.
  • Work as an entertainer.
  • Work as a doctor or dentist in training (unless specifically permitted).

Your right to work is verified by employers using your share code from the UKVI system. Most university campus jobs and part-time retail/hospitality roles are perfectly fine within the 20-hour limit. Because a large Pakistani community and a big student population mean intense competition for campus jobs, start applying early and use the career service rather than relying on the retail sector alone.

Extending and switching your visa

You can apply to extend your Student visa from inside the UK if:

  • You are already in the UK on a Student visa (or the old Tier 4 visa).
  • Your new course begins within 28 days of your current visa expiring.
  • You have a new CAS for the extended course.

How do I extend my Student visa from inside the UK?

You submit a new online application as normal, with a new CAS, a fresh 28-day financial statement, and updated academic documents. The fee is £558 plus a new IHS covering the extended period. Your new course must start within 28 days of your current visa expiring, and you must apply before your current permission runs out.

Can I switch into the Student visa from another UK visa?

You can also switch to a Student visa from inside the UK if you are on certain other visa types (e.g., a Graduate visa, a Standard Visitor visa in some circumstances, or a Short-term Study visa). The application fee for switching or extending is also £558. You cannot simply remain on a visitor visa and start a full-time degree — the switch has to be granted first.

What visa can I move to after I graduate?

After completing your studies, you may be eligible to switch to the Graduate Route, a Skilled Worker visa, or another immigration category, depending on your circumstances. For most Pakistani graduates the sequence is the same: claim the 2-year (or 3-year for a PhD) Graduate Route, use it to build UK experience, then switch to a long-term work route if your salary and occupation qualify.

Common refusal reasons and how to avoid them

Pakistani students face one of the highest refusal rates among UK student visa applicants globally — approximately 32% in the 2024–25 cycle, compared to a global average of around 12%. UKVI operates a risk-scoring system, and Pakistan is classified as a higher-risk origin country based on historical data. The good news is that almost every refusal is caused by avoidable mistakes. Here are the top reasons:

1. Why are financial evidence failures the top reason for refusal (~40%)?

  • The 28-day rule broken: Even a brief dip below the required amount resets the clock. Always maintain a buffer.
  • Unexplained large deposits: Sudden lump sums look like borrowed money. Move funds early and explain the source.
  • Wrong account type: Savings certificates, mutual funds, and credit card limits do not count. Use a standard savings or current account.
  • Unstamped bank statements: Always get official, stamped statements on bank letterhead.
  • Currency conversion shortfall: UKVI uses the exchange rate on the date of application. If the PKR weakens, your balance may fall short. Add a 5–10% buffer.

2. Why are credibility (genuine student) refusals so common (~25%)?

  • Course choice does not match background: If your master's is in a completely different field from your bachelor's, explain the transition clearly.
  • Weak personal statement: Generic, template-style statements are easy to spot. Write specifically about why this course, why this university, and what you will do after returning to Pakistan.
  • Failed credibility interview: If called for an interview, know your course modules, tuition fees, university name, and career plan. Contradicting your application is fatal.
  • Phrases that signal immigration intent: Avoid phrases like "explore opportunities in the UK" or "see what the future holds." Focus on returning to Pakistan and applying your education there.

3. What goes wrong with the CAS itself (~3%)?

  • An expired CAS (more than 6 months old).
  • A mismatched CAS — name, dates, or fees that do not match your application.
  • A withdrawn or spent CAS — each CAS supports only one application.

4. Which missing documents cause refusal (~2%)?

  • No TB test certificate, or an expired one (must be valid within 6 months).
  • No ATAS certificate when one is required.
  • Untranslated documents (anything not in English needs a certified translation).
  • Missing parental consent for under-18 applicants.

5. How do immigration history issues cause refusal (~10%)?

  • Failure to declare a previous visa refusal from any country. UKVI will find it. Non-disclosure is treated as deception.
  • Previous overstays or immigration violations.

6. What is deception, and why is it the worst possible outcome?

If UKVI concludes that you knowingly used false documents or information, you face a mandatory refusal and a 10-year ban on entry clearance applications. This includes fake bank statements, forged employment letters, and fabricated academic records. This outcome is the single worst result in the process — never risk it. A refusal for thin financial evidence costs you a fee and a few months; a deception finding can cost you a decade.

How can I review my application before I submit it?

Run a three-pass check. First, compare every personal detail on your application form against your passport and your CAS character by character. Second, re-add your financial requirement from scratch — CAS tuition minus deposit, plus the correct maintenance rate for your study location times nine — and compare it to your closing balance with the buffer included. Third, ask someone who knows your course whether your stated plan is coherent. Most refusals would have been caught by one of those three passes.

Pakistani-specific tips

These tips address issues that are particularly relevant to applicants from Pakistan, and they come from the mistakes that actually appear in refusal decisions rather than from generic advice.

Should I carry my CNIC during the application?

Carry your CNIC (Computerised National Identity Card) at all times during the application process. Your name on the CNIC must match your passport. If you have changed your name (e.g., after marriage), ensure all documents reflect the current name, and carry supporting evidence (marriage certificate, gazette notification). A mismatch between CNIC, passport and CAS is the kind of detail a caseworker notices immediately.

How do I get a UKVI-compliant bank letter in Pakistan?

Many Pakistani bank statements do not meet UKVI requirements by default. Request an official bank letter that includes: the account holder's name, account number, account type, currency, opening balance, closing balance, and the balance for each day of the statement period. The letter should be on bank letterhead, signed and stamped by a bank officer. Banks such as HBL, MCB, UBL, Alfalah, and Bank Alfalah can provide these — request them at least 2 weeks before you need them.

Do I need HEC attestation of my academic documents?

While UKVI does not always require HEC (Higher Education Commission) attestation of academic documents, some UK universities may request it as part of the CAS process. If your university requires attested documents, get them attested by HEC before sending them. HEC attestation confirms the authenticity of your degree and transcripts. Ask your university for this early, because HEC processing can add weeks that you do not have spare.

Is a NADRA Family Registration Certificate really useful?

If your family is sponsoring you, a NADRA FRC is a powerful supporting document. It officially establishes your family relationship and is recognised by UKVI. You can apply for an FRC online through the NADRA website or visit a NADRA centre. Processing typically takes 5–10 working days, so order it alongside your birth certificate rather than at the last minute.

Does the ranking of my university affect my visa application?

UKVI gives more scrutiny to applications from students going to lower-ranked or less well-known institutions. If possible, choose a Russell Group university or an institution with a strong international reputation. Your visa application is stronger when the university is well-known to the caseworker. You can check whether your university is a licensed student sponsor on the GOV.UK Register of Licensed Sponsors.

How do I protect my application from PKR volatility?

The Pakistani rupee has been volatile against the pound. A bank balance that was sufficient at the start of your 28-day window may fall short by the time you apply if the PKR weakens. Always maintain a buffer of at least 10% above the minimum required amount. Monitor the exchange rate and, if possible, hold funds in GBP or maintain a balance well above the threshold.

When should I book my TB test?

TB tests at UKVI-approved clinics in Pakistan are mandatory for all Student visa applicants staying more than 6 months. Approved clinics include IOM (International Organisation for Migration) clinics in Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi, and other designated facilities. Appointments fill up quickly, especially in the months before the September intake. Book at least 3–4 weeks before you need the certificate. The certificate is valid for 6 months — ensure it remains valid when you submit your visa application.

What should I expect from a credibility interview?

In 2026, credibility interviews are more common for Pakistani applicants. If called for one (by phone or in person), be prepared to discuss:

  • Why you chose this specific course and university
  • What modules you will study
  • How the course connects to your career goals in Pakistan
  • How you will fund your studies
  • What your plans are after graduation (return to Pakistan)

Do not memorise scripted answers. Speak naturally and honestly. If your answers contradict your personal statement, that is a red flag.

Scams to avoid

The UK student visa process attracts scams targeting hopeful students and their families, and Pakistani applicants are targeted repeatedly because the stakes feel high and the deadlines feel urgent. Be aware of:

How do I spot a fake or unlicensed agent?

Many so-called "education consultants" in Pakistan are not licensed or regulated. They may:

  • Promise a guaranteed visa — no one can guarantee a visa. Only UKVI makes that decision.
  • Charge excessive fees for services that you can do yourself (filling out the online application, booking a VFS appointment).
  • Submit fabricated documents (fake bank statements, fake employment letters) — this leads to refusal and a 10-year ban.
  • Tell you to hide previous refusals — UKVI will find them, and hiding them is treated as deception.

If you want professional help, use an adviser registered with the OISC (Office of the Immigration Services Commissioner) in the UK, or a solicitor regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA). You can verify registration on the OISC or SRA websites. For Pakistani-based consultants, ask for their track record, ask to see reviews, and never hand over original documents.

Are fake bank statements ever worth the risk?

Some agents offer to "arrange" bank statements or employment letters. UKVI verifies financial evidence directly with banks, especially for Pakistani and Nigerian applicants. A fake statement will be detected, leading to refusal and potentially a 10-year ban for deception. Never use fabricated documents. If you cannot meet the financial requirement legitimately, wait and save longer rather than attempting to manufacture evidence.

What about phishing emails claiming to be from UKVI or VFS?

Be wary of emails claiming to be from UKVI, VFS Global, or a UK university asking for payment or personal information. Official communications come through the GOV.UK portal or your university's official email. Never share your UKVI account password or payment details in response to an unsolicited email. Legitimate UKVI messages ask you to sign in through gov.uk rather than to follow links in an email.

Can I buy or reserve a VFS appointment slot?

Some people claim to sell or reserve VFS Global appointment slots. VFS appointments are booked through the official VFS Global website after you have submitted your online application and paid the fees. There is no legitimate secondary market for appointment slots. Book directly through the official portal. Paying for a "reserved slot" is both a scam and a way to end up with a non-attending applicant in your place.

Applying with dependants

Under rules tightened in January 2024, most Student visa holders can no longer bring dependants (spouse or children) unless:

  • You are studying a PhD or other doctoral research programme, or
  • You are a government-sponsored student studying for a course longer than 6 months.

What must each dependant prove and pay?

If you do qualify to bring dependants, each dependant must:

  • Pay their own visa application fee (£558).
  • Pay their own IHS at the student rate (£776 per year).
  • Show maintenance funds of £845 per month (London) or £680 per month (outside London) for up to 9 months, in addition to your own maintenance funds.
  • Provide evidence of the relationship (marriage certificate, birth certificate for children).

My course is a master's, not a PhD — can I bring my family?

Almost certainly not. Unless you are a government-sponsored student on a course longer than 6 months, the January 2024 changes mean dependants are refused for master's and bachelor's students. Plan your family's immigration separately, because a dependant refusal affects the main applicant too and can result in your own visa being varied or cancelled.

Where do I check the current dependant rules?

Rules in this area have changed more than once, so verify before you make plans. If you are unsure whether you qualify to bring dependants, check the latest rules on gov.uk/student-visa/family-members. Also confirm with your university in writing whether your programme is a qualifying doctoral research programme, because that classification decides your eligibility.

The Graduate Route — what happens after you study

After completing your degree, you may be eligible for the Graduate Route visa, which allows you to stay in the UK and work (or look for work) for:

  • 2 years — if you completed a bachelor's or master's degree.
  • 3 years — if you completed a PhD or other doctoral qualification.

How much does the Graduate Route cost?

The Graduate Route is a one-time, non-extendable visa. The application fee is £937 (as of 2026), plus the standard IHS rate of £1,035 per year (the non-student rate). You must apply from within the UK before your Student visa expires, so diarise the date your Student permission ends well before you start job hunting.

What can I do on the Graduate Route?

During the Graduate Route, you can work full-time in any job, switch employers, and be self-employed. That last point is worth emphasising: self-employment is prohibited on a Student visa but permitted on the Graduate Route, which is why some Pakistani graduates start freelancing or consultancy work as soon as they convert.

Can I extend the Graduate Route or change my sponsor?

No. The Graduate Route cannot be extended and is not a route to settlement in itself. After it expires you would need to switch to another visa category (e.g., Skilled Worker visa) to stay, and you cannot use it to move to a different university sponsor. Treat it as a work window, not a way to keep studying in the UK.

Troubleshooting and additional scenarios

What should I do if my UK student visa from Pakistan is refused?

You have two options:

  • Administrative review: You can request an administrative review of the decision for a fee of £80. This is a paper review — no new evidence can be submitted. It is only worthwhile if you believe UKVI made a clear error in applying the rules. Administrative review takes approximately 28 days.
  • Reapply: In most cases, the better option is to fix the problem and reapply with a new CAS. Address the specific reason for refusal (e.g., correct the financial evidence, obtain a new TB test, rewrite your personal statement), get a fresh CAS from the university, and submit a new application with the £558 fee again.

If your refusal was on the ground of deception, take professional legal advice immediately. A 10-year ban may be in play. A refusal is disappointing but recoverable; a deception finding changes the nature of the problem entirely, and the cost of a short consultation is trivial compared to the stakes.

What if my course gets deferred to a later intake?

If your university defers your course to a later intake, your CAS will be cancelled and a new one will be issued for the new start date. You must wait for the new CAS before applying for your visa. The 28-day financial window must align with the new application date. A deferral is usually a delay rather than a refusal, so use the extra months to build a cleaner financial history.

What if I change university after receiving my CAS?

If you switch to a different UK university after receiving a CAS, your original CAS is no longer valid. You need a new CAS from the new university. Inform your original university so they can cancel the CAS on the UKVI system, and if you already submitted an application, withdraw it rather than leaving it running against a spent CAS.

Can I apply if I have a previous UK visa refusal?

Yes, but you must declare the refusal on your application. A previous refusal does not automatically bar you from obtaining a Student visa — but you need to address the reason for the previous refusal and explain why the circumstances have changed. Non-disclosure of a previous refusal is treated as deception and carries far heavier consequences than the original refusal.

What if my TB test certificate expires before I apply?

Book a new test. A TB certificate is valid for 6 months from the date of the test, and an expired one is treated as a missing document. Approved clinics in Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi can usually turn an appointment around in a week, but leave enough margin before your application date, and re-check that the clinic is on the UKVI-approved list.

What if my bank statement is more than 31 days old?

Request a fresh stamped statement. The 28-day period must end within 31 days of your application date, so an older statement makes your financial evidence invalid regardless of how much money you hold. This is a common problem for applicants who prepare documents in a batch weeks ahead of time — always collect the bank statement last, just before you apply.

Summary: your 2026 UK Student visa action plan

Here is a condensed checklist you can print and tick off as you go. Work through it in order rather than in parallel, because almost every item depends on the one before it:

  1. ☐ Receive unconditional offer from a UK licensed sponsor university.
  2. ☐ Accept offer, pay deposit, request CAS.
  3. ☐ Verify all CAS details match your passport and course information.
  4. ☐ Take IELTS UKVI (or equivalent SELT) if required.
  5. ☐ Get TB test from a UKVI-approved clinic in Pakistan.
  6. ☐ Obtain ATAS certificate if your course requires one.
  7. ☐ Ensure funds are in eligible account for at least 28 consecutive days.
  8. ☐ Get official stamped bank statements (or sponsor's statements + consent letter).
  9. ☐ Prepare all supporting documents (academic, personal, sponsor).
  10. ☐ Write a strong, specific personal statement.
  11. ☐ Complete the online application at gov.uk/student-visa/apply.
  12. ☐ Pay visa fee (£558) and IHS (£776/year) online.
  13. ☐ Book biometrics appointment at VFS Global (Islamabad, Lahore, or Karachi).
  14. ☐ Attend appointment, submit biometrics and documents.
  15. ☐ Wait for decision (~3 weeks standard).
  16. ☐ If approved: link passport to UKVI account, prepare for travel.
  17. ☐ Enter the UK up to 1 month before your course starts.
  18. ☐ Enrol at your university and begin your studies.

How long should the whole plan take from start to finish?

Roughly six to nine months. The longest pole is the university application and English testing stage, followed by the 28-day financial window, then a three-week (sometimes six-week) decision period.

What is the single biggest risk to my application?

The financial evidence, by a wide margin. Around 40% of Pakistani refusals trace back to money documentation rather than to academic ability or intentions. Get the account right, get the balance right, get the 28 days right, and get the stamp on the statement right — and you remove the most likely reason for failure before you ever submit.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a UK student visa cost from Pakistan in 2026?

As of 8 April 2026, the Student visa application fee is £558 per applicant. On top of that you pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) at £776 per year of your visa, plus approximately PKR 10,000–17,000 for the TB test and roughly PKR 50,000–80,000 for your IELTS UKVI test. Budget for all of these before you begin. For a 1-year master's, total visa-related costs (excluding tuition) are approximately £1,334–£2,110 in visa fees and IHS alone.

How much bank balance is required for a UK student visa from Pakistan?

You must show your first-year tuition fees (as stated on your CAS, minus any deposit already paid) plus living costs of £1,529 per month if studying in London or £1,171 per month if outside London, for up to 9 months. That means a maximum of £13,761 for London or £10,539 for outside London, on top of any unpaid tuition. Funds must sit in your account (or a parent's account) for 28 consecutive days ending within 31 days of your application. Always add a 5–10% buffer for currency fluctuation.

How long does the UK student visa take to process from Pakistan?

Standard processing is approximately 3 weeks (15 working days) from the date UKVI receives your biometrics. During peak season (June–September) it can take 4–6 weeks. Priority processing (around 5 working days) is available for an extra fee of approximately £500 if offered at your VFS centre. Super-priority (next working day) may be available for about £1,000. Always apply early — at least 8–10 weeks before your course starts.

Can I work in the UK as a student?

Yes. If you hold a Student visa, you can work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full-time during official vacation periods (including the summer break). You cannot be self-employed, fill a permanent full-time vacancy, or work as a professional sportsperson or sports coach. Your right to work is verified by employers using your UKVI share code. After graduation, the Graduate Route allows you to work full-time for 2 years (3 years for PhD graduates).

What is the CAS number and do I need it?

CAS stands for Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies. It is an electronic record issued by your UK university once you accept an unconditional offer and meet all conditions (including paying any required deposit). It contains a unique 14-character reference number that you must enter in your visa application. Without a valid CAS, you cannot apply for a Student visa. Your CAS is valid for 6 months from the date it is assigned, and it can only be used once.

Do I need an IELTS certificate for a UK student visa from Pakistan?

You need to demonstrate English at roughly CEFR B2, and an IELTS for UKVI result is the most widely accepted way to do it. Most Pakistani universities want an overall 6.0–6.5 with no band below 5.5–6.0. If your university assessed your English itself and recorded that on your CAS, a separate visa-purpose test may not be required — check your CAS rather than paying for a test you do not need.

Can I apply from inside Pakistan or from inside the UK?

You apply from Pakistan through a VFS Global centre — Islamabad, Lahore or Karachi — as an "Apply from outside the UK" applicant. You can also apply from inside the UK to extend or switch, and the fee is the same £558 either way. The 12-month in-country financial evidence exemption only applies to people already holding UK permission for at least 12 months, which does not help first-time applicants in Pakistan.

What is the minimum bank balance in Pakistani rupees?

It depends entirely on your tuition fee. The formula is your CAS tuition minus any deposit paid, plus £1,171 × 9 for outside London (or £1,529 × 9 for London). In the worked Manchester example above, the requirement was £23,539. Convert that at a conservative rate, add 10%, and check the GBP figures on gov.uk before you finalise the number.

Can my father sponsor my UK student visa from Pakistan application?

Yes, and this is the most common arrangement. You need his signed consent letter naming you, your passport number, the university and the course, plus a birth certificate or NADRA FRC, his CNIC, his own 28-day stamped bank statement, and evidence of his income or wealth. Remember that the maintenance rate is based on your study location, not his, and that only the tuition balance still owed on the CAS counts as tuition.

Is the UK student visa from Pakistan refundable if it is refused?

No. The £558 application fee and the IHS are both non-refundable once paid, regardless of the outcome. The only fee you might recover in practice is the £80 administrative review fee if you win a review, which is a narrow scenario. Treat the visa costs as a fixed cost of applying rather than a deposit.

Is a tuberculosis test required for everyone from Pakistan?

Yes, for anyone applying from Pakistan on a Student visa for a stay longer than 6 months, which covers almost all degree courses. The test must be done at a UKVI-approved clinic — IOM clinics in Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi among them — and the certificate is valid for 6 months. Book it 3–4 weeks before you need it, and check the approved clinic list rather than assuming any lab will do.

Can I take my wife and children with me on a UK student visa from Pakistan?

Only if you are a PhD or other doctoral research student, or a government-sponsored student on a course longer than 6 months. For most Pakistani master's and bachelor's applicants, dependants are no longer permitted. Each dependant who is allowed would need their own £558 fee, their own IHS, an additional £845/month (London) or £680/month (outside London) in maintenance, and proof of the relationship.

UK Student Visa from Pakistan: Documents & Fees: what this guide covers

This guide explains everything a Pakistani student needs to know about UK student visa from Pakistan, including eligibility, costs, timelines and practical steps. Use the sections above to find the exact information you need, or bookmark this page and return as your application progresses. Every fee, threshold and rule quoted here is the 2026 position, so check the official source before you commit money.

Final thoughts

Applying for a UK Student visa from Pakistan in 2026 is a multi-step process that demands careful planning, meticulous documentation, and genuine engagement with your study plans. The fee increase to £558, the higher maintenance thresholds of £1,529/£1,171 per month, and the intensified credibility assessment all mean that Pakistani applicants cannot afford to cut corners. But the process is straightforward when you approach it methodically: get your CAS early, maintain your funds with a buffer, prepare every document to UKVI standards, write a personal statement that is authentically yours, and submit your application well ahead of your course start date.

The UK remains one of the best places in the world to study, with institutions that are globally recognised, a post-study work route that gives you real career flexibility, and a multicultural society that includes one of the largest Pakistani diasporas in the world. Thousands of Pakistani students successfully obtain their visas every year. With proper preparation, you can be one of them.

What should I do first if I am starting from zero today?

Start your university applications immediately, because everything else depends on them. While offers are coming in, sit a UKVI-approved English test and book a TB test. Only request your CAS once you have accepted an offer and your funding plan is realistic, and do not touch the 28-day money window until your documents are otherwise ready.

Where can I learn more about studying in the UK and funding my degree?

For more information on studying in the UK, scholarships available to Pakistani students, and step-by-step guides to other study-abroad destinations, explore the rest of AbroadReady. We are here to help you every step of the way.

Where can I verify the official 2026 requirements before I apply?

Disclaimer: UK Visas and Immigration rules, fees, and requirements are reviewed regularly. Always verify current requirements on gov.uk/student-visa before applying. This guide reflects rules and fees in force as of August 2026. Figures marked "confirm on gov.uk" should be double-checked against the official source at the time of your application.

posts.metaDescription: US F-1 student visa from Pakistan 2026 guide: How Pakistani students can get an F-1 student visa for the USA in 2026: I-20, SEVIS fee, DS-160, financial documents,
posts.excerpt: A full F-1 visa guide for Pakistan: I-20 and SEVIS fee, DS-160 form, DS-160 appointment at the US embassy, bank statement rules, interview questions and processing timeline.
posts.bodyHtml:
What is the US F-1 student visa from Pakistan, and why does it feel so hard?

Securing a US F-1 student visa from Pakistan is one of the most important steps in your study-abroad journey, and it is also the step that causes the most anxiety. Every year thousands of Pakistani students receive admission offers from American universities, but the visa process — with its multiple fees, strict documentation requirements, and face-to-face embassy interview — can feel opaque and intimidating. The paperwork is long, the rules are published across several government websites, and the decision is made by a consular officer you will meet for a few minutes. That combination is why the process feels heavier than it is.

How does this guide help me?

This guide is written specifically for Pakistani students in 2026. It walks you through every stage, from receiving your I-20 to standing in front of a consular officer in Islamabad, Karachi or Lahore, with concrete figures, realistic timelines and practical advice that reflects how the process actually works on the ground in Pakistan. Rather than a wall of prose, it is organised as questions and answers, so you can jump straight to the step you are stuck on: the DS-160, the SEVIS fee, the money, the appointment, or the interview answers themselves.

Is the process different for community colleges, state universities and Ivy League campuses?

Whether you are an undergraduate heading to a community college in California, a master's student joining a research programme at a state university in Texas, or a PhD applicant heading to an Ivy League campus in the northeast, the F-1 visa process is essentially the same. What changes is the strength of your financial documentation, the depth of your preparation for the interview, and the way you present your ties to Pakistan. This guide covers all of it in detail.

How long should I allow for the whole process?

Allow three to four months from the moment your I-20 arrives to the day you board a flight. That window covers paying the SEVIS I-901 fee, completing and submitting the DS-160, paying the MRV fee through HBL, securing an appointment slot at one of the three mission locations, attending the interview, and waiting for your passport to be returned with the visa stamp. Students who start assembling financial evidence and booking appointments in the same month their I-20 arrives usually find the pace comfortable. Students who wait until the week of departure usually find the appointment calendar closed in front of them.

What do successful Pakistani applicants do differently?

They arrive with one consistent story that every document supports. Their name matches across the passport, the DS-160 and the I-20. Their bank statements show the same income that their sponsor's employment letter describes. Their chosen university has a specific reason attached to it, not a ranking. And their answer about the future is a plan with a city, an industry and a job title in Pakistan. Nothing about the US F-1 student visa from Pakistan is mysterious; it is simply a consistency test.

Key takeaways

What are the most important things to know before I start?

  • The F-1 visa is a nonimmigrant student visa for full-time study at a SEVP-certified US school. You apply after receiving your Form I-20.
  • In 2026 the SEVIS I-901 fee is $350 for new F-1 students (confirm on fmjfee.com) and the MRV visa application fee is $185 (confirm on travel.state.gov).
  • You must complete the DS-160 online application, pay both fees, book an appointment, and attend an in-person interview at the US Embassy in Islamabad or a US consulate in Karachi or Lahore.
  • Financial evidence must match or exceed the total cost of attendance listed on your I-20. Pakistani students typically show six months of bank statements, sponsor letters, property documents, and employment verification.
  • The consular officer evaluates your nonimmigrant intent under Section 214(b) of the Immigration and Nationality Act — you must demonstrate strong ties to Pakistan and a clear plan to return after studies.
  • Processing after a successful interview is usually 3–5 business days, but administrative processing can take weeks. Apply early — ideally three to four months before your programme starts.
  • Beware of visa agents and fraudulent websites. The official appointment system is through ustraveldocs.com/pk. No agent can guarantee a visa.

Understanding the F-1 Visa: What It Is and Who It Is For

What exactly is the F-1 nonimmigrant visa?

The F-1 nonimmigrant visa is the standard visa issued to international students who want to pursue full-time academic studies in the United States. It is governed by Section 101(a)(15)(F) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, and it covers study at colleges, universities, conservatories, seminaries, language training programmes, and other academic institutions that are certified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP). The word that matters is academic. The F-1 exists to let you take a credited course of study, which is why it is tied to a specific school, a specific programme and a specific set of dates on your Form I-20.

Who qualifies for a US F-1 student visa from Pakistan?

If you have been accepted by a US institution and that institution has issued you a Form I-20, you are eligible to apply for an F-1 visa. The F-1 is specifically for academic study — if you are coming to the US for vocational or non-academic training, a different visa category (M-1) applies. For the vast majority of Pakistani students heading to American universities, the F-1 is the correct and only option. Eligibility, however, is only the entry requirement. The officer still assesses whether you can fund the programme and whether you intend to leave after it, so being eligible on paper does not guarantee approval.

Which other US visa categories exist, and how do they compare?

It is worth understanding where the F-1 sits among US visa categories, because some Pakistani students confuse it with other options:
